subject: Using SAS or Python to calculate individual point density

messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: Using SAS or Python to calculate individual point density
parts:
James (and list):

I'm not completely sure this answers your question, but if you consult
the Distance Users Guide, Appendix - MCDS Engine Reference, you will
learn about a Stats file that is created by Distance. That file can be
accessed, and the global detection function (along with its measures of
uncertainty) can be read by whatever bits and pieces of software you
wish. Searching the PDF for 'stats file' will reveal great amounts of
detail about this file, its specification, and format.

This engine, named "multiple covariate distance sampling" engine is your
friend for fitting the covariates of interest to you in the detection
function.

messages.author: 7915d3b1c6db79b6
messages.subject: Using SAS or Python to calculate individual point density
parts:
Hello Folks,

I am interested in taking a global detection probability function from
program Distance into another program such as SAS or Python and
computing density for each one of my samples (point transects). Has
anyone ever done this? I would like to incorporate numerous covariates
into the model as well. I envision it being able to be dynamic such
that the detection probabilities for each of my intervals can be
changed. Any suggestions would be appreciated!

Thank you.

james martin
